newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Thursday on overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
LME copper at one stage dived to a low of $2,285 after further falls in the price of zinc. But by the close of business three months copper bounced to $2,305.
Prices were expected to come under pressured following the poor chart close, and could test support at $2,250, London analysts said.
Shanghai's most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 20,780 yuan ($2,506) per tonne, losing 340 yuan per tonne.
It opened at 20,700 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 20,810 yuan per tonne and a low of 20,650 yuan per tonne.
August fell 250 to 20,550 yuan, September 180 to 20,650, October 320 to 20,700, December 350 to 20,800 and the January 1997 contract 300 to 20,770 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 74,980 tonnes from 88,140 tonnes.
Copper opened lower and was saved by some speculative buying and short-covering at low levels early in the session, traders said.
But it fell again late in the session due to heavy selling pressure above the 20,800-yuan level, they said.
Trader said the overnight LME losses had shaken buying interest in Shanghai, where many investors liquidated long positions.
"Heavy selling was seen above the 20,800 yuan level today, which pushed prices down," one trader said.
"Longs tried to push up later-maturing contracts to boost market sentiment, but follow-up buying was limited," another trader said.
Shanghai physical copper fell to around 20,700 yuan per tonne, from 20,850/20,900 in the morning as slack consumption, typical of the summer months, prevailed traders said.
Traders said LME would be an important influence on Shanghai copper in an absence of domestic market-moving news.
Aluminium ended down. August fell 50 to 13,850 yuan per tonne, September 120 to 13,960, October 180 to 13,950, November 270 to 13,980 and December 300 to 14,000 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 4,580 tonnes from 2,840 tonnes.
